findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add explicit input-selection guidance for the description discriminator: specify that the test input must produce a DC-truncated result (≤ 32767 plain chars) whose ADF serialization exceeds 32000 chars, and add a discriminator assertion such as `assert len(json.dumps(adf_module.text_to_adf(dc_truncated_body))) > 32000` immediately after computing the pass-2 snapshot body, so a reviewer can confirm the discriminator region is actually exercised.
evidence: Plan: 'DC fits plain characters at WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32767), while Cloud fits ADF-SERIALIZED size at _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32000). Those genuinely differ, so a length/ADF-shape assertion here would FAIL if the fallback supplied Cloud's mapper'
adf.py:332-360: `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000`; `fit_text_to_adf_limit` binary-searches for the largest prefix fitting within 32000 ADF chars
rich_text.py:91-94: DC's `fit_outbound` truncates at 32767 plain chars unconditionally
No input-selection guidance or discriminator assertion is stated in the plan
findings.finding: The description-discriminator AC requires a test input for which DC's truncation (at 32767 plain chars) produces a result that Cloud's mapper would NOT converge against — i.e. the DC-truncated 32767-char string must serialize to > 32000 ADF chars so that Cloud's path would truncate it further and still emit a second-pass mutation. The plan mandates this discriminator but gives no guidance on input selection or a verification assertion to confirm the discriminator fires. For a 1-line 32768-char input of repeated 'X', the ADF serialization of the 32767-char DC-truncated result is approximately `len(json.dumps({'type':'doc','version':1,'content':[{'type':'paragraph','content':[{'type':'text','text':'X'*32738+' … [truncated by reconciler]'}]}]}))` ≈ 32807 chars, which exceeds 32000 — so the discriminator DOES fire for this input. But an implementer who picks a different input (e.g. a very short oversize string) may not trigger the region where DC and Cloud diverge, making the discriminator AC vacuously satisfied.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'the DESCRIPTION test proves it exercised DC's fit by a VALUE-BASED discriminator'
scenarios: Implementer uses a 33000-char input: DC truncates to 32767 chars; Cloud truncates to ~20000 chars (to fit ADF ≤ 32000). A snapshot built from the DC-truncated body would cause Cloud's path to emit a second-pass mutation (32767-char body serializes to ~32807 ADF chars > 32000). DC's path would NOT emit. Discriminator fires correctly.

Implementer uses a 32800-char input of a single short line: DC truncates to 32767 chars; that 32767-char single-line body may serialize to only ~32825 ADF chars — still > 32000 — discriminator fires. But an implementer who doesn't verify this assumption may use an input where it doesn't.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach step 2 or the description-discriminator AC: 'Choose an oversize input of at least 33 000 plain characters. After DC truncation at 32767, assert `len(json.dumps(text_to_adf(dc_truncated_body))) > 32000` — this confirms the discriminator is in the active region where DC and Cloud would diverge. This assertion is also the mutation check: if Cloud's mapper ran instead (truncating to ~20 000 chars to fit ADF ≤ 32000), the pass-2 snapshot would not match and a mutation would be emitted, turning the convergence assertion red.'

Without knowing whether the project uses mutmut, cosmic-ray, a manual delete-and-rerun convention, or a CI mutation gate, an executor cannot produce verifiable evidence that each mutation check passed. The ACs read as assertions ('turns the DC cells RED') rather than reproducible commands.

scenarios: An executor completes the test files, all CI tests pass, but skips the mutation verification entirely because there is no stated procedure — the ACs appear satisfied on paper while the injection-path coverage is unverified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that the comment sanitizer check MUST use the recorder approach (not identity assertion): wrap `_DCSanitizer` in a recording wrapper before passing it as `sanitizer=` and assert `recorder.fit_comment_called` after the call — the identity approach is not executable because `_diff_comments` stores the resolved sanitizer as a local variable and returns no evidence of which object ran.
evidence: outbound_comments.py:208: `sanitizer = _resolve_sanitizer(sanitizer)` — resolved sanitizer is a local variable, not returned or stored
Plan: 'e.g. wrap it in a recorder and assert the recorder observed the call, or assert identity against dc_backend.sanitizer'

Both Cloud and DC sanitizers produce byte-identical output (same limit, same suffix, verified in comment_limits.py:69 and rich_text.py:93), so a post-call value check is also impossible — the ONLY viable approach is the recorder
findings.finding: The plan offers 'assert identity against `dc_backend.sanitizer`' as a co-equal alternative to the recorder approach for the comment sanitizer check, but this approach is not executable as a meaningful post-call assertion: `_diff_comments` stores the resolved sanitizer as a local variable (`sanitizer = _resolve_sanitizer(sanitizer)` at outbound_comments.py:208) and returns nothing about which object ran. A pre-call `assert injected is dc_backend.sanitizer` is trivially true by construction and proves nothing about whether the fallback fired. Only the recorder/wrapper approach (intercept `fit_comment` and verify it was called) can actually verify that the DC sanitizer ran rather than Cloud's. Presenting both as equivalent leaves the implementer likely to attempt the identity assertion, find it proves nothing, and either ship a vacuous check or become confused.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'the COMMENT test proves it exercised DC's sanitizer by an IDENTITY or RECORDING check' and 'assert identity against dc_backend.sanitizer'
scenarios: Implementer attempts `assert dc_backend.sanitizer is <object passed to _diff_comments>` — trivially true by construction, never fails, proves nothing if the fallback silently substituted Cloud's sanitizer
Implementer ships a no-op identity assertion that always passes whether the DC sanitizer or Cloud's sanitizer ran inside _diff_comments, defeating the mutation-check AC entirely
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'or assert identity against `dc_backend.sanitizer`' with: 'use a recorder wrapper — e.g. `class RecordingSanitizer: def __init__(self, inner): self._inner = inner; self.called = False; def fit_comment(self, b): self.called = True; return self._inner.fit_comment(b)` — pass it as `sanitizer=recorder` and assert `recorder.called` after the call. The identity assertion approach is not viable: `_diff_comments` resolves the sanitizer into a local variable and the caller has no post-call access to which object ran.'
